lang: Hebrew (English summary pp. 137-138 included in the PDF)
location_note: East of the Siloam Pool, against the outer face of its eastern dam wall, City of David; map ref. 22235-6/63072-3 (NIG; Hebrew text and English summary).
notes: 2009 rescue excavation. Dam wall W1 established no later than the end of the First Temple period and replastered three times (plaster typical of the Second Temple period); plastered pool built against it during the Great Revolt; plastered channel L103 through the dam linking the Siloam Pool to the new pool, filled in the second half of the 1st c. CE. The Siloam Pool itself is named, not excavated here; not coded. Plaster date: see ATQ101-079.

features.subtype: inclined dam wall W1 (c. 50 m long, 3.5 m wide) enclosing the Siloam Pool on the east, plaster phases a-c
features.period: established no later than the 7th-early 6th c. BCE; plastered and in use in the Second Temple period
features.quote: outer face of the inclined eastern side of the dam was exposed

features.subtype: Plastered Pool (L102, L104; 8.4 x 3 x 3.1 m) built against the dam's outer face
features.period: constructed during the Great Revolt (later 1st c. CE coins in its foundation), filled soon after
features.quote: the Plastered Pool was constructed during the Great Revolt

features.subtype: plastered drainage channel L103 through the dam carrying excess water from the Siloam Pool to the Plastered Pool
features.period: in use until filled in the second half of the 1st c. CE
features.quote: A drainage channel traversing the dam wall and connecting the two pools
